questions.enonce_markdown: In the Covenant between God and Abraham the following promises were conspicuous except;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the accounts of the covenant with Abraham (Genesis 12, 15 and 17), the promises that stand out are the gift of a land (Canaan), many descendants (a great nation) and blessing (God blesses Abraham so that he becomes a blessing to others). Land, blessing and descendants are therefore the conspicuous promises. Protection is not one of the three headline promises of the covenant, even though God also describes himself as Abraham's shield in Genesis 15. It is therefore the option that does not belong.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - abraham and the covenant

questions.enonce_markdown: The name of Abraham's most trusted servant was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Genesis 15:2 names Eliezer of Damascus as the servant who was to be Abraham's heir if he had no son, and Jewish and Christian tradition identifies him with the trusted servant sent to find a wife for Isaac in Genesis 24. Haran and Nahor are members of Abraham's family (a brother and another relative of the same generation), and Elisha is a prophet who lived many centuries later.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - abraham and the covenant

questions.enonce_markdown: Who received Issac's blessing?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Genesis 27 Isaac, old and blind, intended to give the blessing of the firstborn to Esau, but Rebekah and Jacob arranged for Jacob to receive it, and Isaac could not take it back. Jacob is therefore the one who received Isaac's blessing. Esau, who lost it, received only a lesser word from his father afterwards. Joseph is Jacob's son and Laban is Jacob's uncle and father-in-law.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - patriarchs of israel

questions.enonce_markdown: The following women were married to Jacob except:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Jacob married the sisters Leah and Rachel, the daughters of Laban, and he also had children by Bilhah, Rachel's maid, who was given to him as a wife (Genesis 29 and 30). Rebecca (Rebekah) was not Jacob's wife: she was the wife of Isaac and the mother of Jacob and Esau. She is therefore the exception.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - patriarchs of israel

questions.enonce_markdown: Joseph's brothers sold him into Egypt in order to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Genesis 37 Joseph's brothers hated him because their father loved him more and because of his dreams, in which they would bow down to him. When they sold him to traders going to Egypt, their aim was to get rid of him and so defeat the dreams, that is, to frustrate his plans. They did receive silver, but money was a by-product and not the motive that drove the story. The other two options are not motives given in the text.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - patriarchs of israel

questions.enonce_markdown: The adventure of Jacob's children into Egypt was primarily to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A severe famine affected Canaan, and Jacob sent his sons to Egypt because grain could be bought there (Genesis 42). The brothers did meet Joseph, but they did not know who he was, so seeing him was not the purpose of the journey. The primary aim was to buy grain.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - patriarchs of israel

questions.enonce_markdown: Which land was given to Jacob and his family in Egypt?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Goshen in the Nile delta, a region suited to their flocks (Genesis 45 to 47). The other names are either Egyptian cities or general descriptions. Genesis 47:11 does speak of the district of Rameses, but the settlement of Jacob's family is classically identified with Goshen.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - patriarchs of israel

questions.enonce_markdown: The last plague before the Passover in Egypt had to do with:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plagues of locusts, darkness and hail came earlier in the sequence of Exodus 7 to 10. The tenth and last plague, which led to the Passover and the release of the Israelites, was the death of the firstborn of Egypt (Exodus 11 and 12), while the Israelites, who had marked their doors with blood, were spared.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - exodus and moses

questions.enonce_markdown: How many tablets of stones did Moses receive from Yahweh on Mount Sinai?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Exodus 31:18 and 34:1 speak of two tablets of stone on which the commandments were written. The number ten refers to the commandments (the Decalogue), not to the number of tablets, and this is the usual trap of the question.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - sinai covenant and law

questions.enonce_markdown: He grew up in Eli's house at Shiloh:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Samuel was dedicated to the Lord by his mother Hannah and brought up in the sanctuary at Shiloh under the priest Eli (1 Samuel 1 to 3). Saul, Jesse and David have no link with Eli's household at Shiloh.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judges and the monarchy

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the father-in-law of Moses?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Moses married Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, who is called Jethro (Exodus 2 and 3, and Exodus 18). Aaron was Moses' brother, Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt, and Jochebed (printed here as Jochebeb) was Moses' mother.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - exodus and moses

questions.enonce_markdown:
He laid the foundation for a Temple in Jerusalem:

*Options as printed:* A) David   B) Saul   C) Solomon   D) Samuel
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Temple in Jerusalem was built by Solomon, who began the work and laid its foundation (1 Kings 5 and 6). David had planned it and gathered materials for it (1 Chronicles 22 and 28), so the phrase 'laid the foundation' can be understood in two ways, as the preparation (David) or as the construction (Solomon). Saul and Samuel had no part in it. The most usual reading, which is the intended one here, is Solomon.

**Intended answer: C (Solomon).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - david and the united kingdom

questions.enonce_markdown: The king who requested wisdom from God to rule his people was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At Gibeon, God invited the young Solomon to ask for whatever he wished, and he asked for an understanding mind to govern the people and to distinguish good from evil (1 Kings 3). God was pleased with this request. Saul, Ahab and David are not the kings associated with this account.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - david and the united kingdom

questions.enonce_markdown: The marriage of Hosea to Gomer signifies:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Hosea 1 to 3 the prophet is told to marry Gomer, a woman who is unfaithful to him, and his marriage becomes a living picture of the relationship between God and Israel: God is the faithful husband and Israel the unfaithful wife who follows other gods. It is therefore a symbol of the bond between God and his people, and not an ideal or a model marriage.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - prophets of israel and judah

choix.texte: A symbol between God and Israel

questions.enonce_markdown:
God's judgment on Jerusalem and Judah in Isaiah was because:

*Options as printed:* A) The leaders have ruined God's Vineyard   B) The women of Zion have sinned   C) The righteous have gone astray   D) The children of Zion were crying
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Isaiah 3 and 5 the people are compared to God's vineyard, and the elders and leaders are accused of having ruined it by injustice and by oppressing the poor (Isaiah 3:14). This is the best known reason given for the judgment on Jerusalem and Judah. Isaiah 3 also condemns the pride of the women of Zion, so option B has some support in the text, and for that reason the question is not reliable enough for automatic marking. Options C and D are not reasons given in the book.

**Intended answer: A (The leaders have ruined God's Vineyard).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - prophets of israel and judah

questions.enonce_markdown: The call of Jeremiah was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Jeremiah 1:5, God knew Jeremiah and set him apart before he was born, and appointed him a prophet to the nations. In Jeremiah 1:10 his task is described both as uprooting and tearing down, destroying and overthrowing, and as building and planting. Option A, which joins the call before birth with the tasks of building and destroying, is the one that matches the text. The other options give details (age 40, nightfall) which the book does not contain.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - prophets of israel and judah

choix.texte: Before his birth to build and destroy

questions.enonce_markdown: An extreme nationalistic Jewish Sect was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Zealots were a Jewish movement of the first century CE which wanted to drive out the Romans by force, and they were extreme in their nationalism. The Sadducees were the priestly and aristocratic party, the Pharisees were teachers of the Law who stressed its careful observance, and the Herodians supported the family of Herod.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: This group believed in the existence of life after death:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Pharisees believed in the resurrection of the dead, in angels and in life after death, while the Sadducees rejected these beliefs (see Acts 23:8). The Scribes were experts in the Law, and the Zionists belong to a modern political movement.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: Qumran as a location is associated with:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Qumran is a site near the north-western shore of the Dead Sea, close to the caves where the Dead Sea Scrolls were found from 1947 onwards. The scrolls are associated with a Jewish community living there. The option is printed 'The Death Sea Scrolls' and means the Dead Sea Scrolls. The Temple was in Jerusalem, and the Mishnah is a collection of rabbinic teaching.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: The " Thirteen Principles of Faith" provides an authoritative summary of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Thirteen Principles of Faith were formulated by the medieval scholar Moses Maimonides as a summary of the essential beliefs of Judaism, such as belief in one God, in the Torah as given by God, in the coming of the Messiah and in the resurrection of the dead. They are therefore a statement of Jewish beliefs, and not a list of writings or customs.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown:
At 30, Buddha abandoned luxury in search of:

*Options as printed:* A) Sickness and sufferings   B) Morality and ethics   C) Truth and knowledge   D) Religion and light
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama left his palace life, his luxury and his family to look for the answer to the problem of suffering that he had seen in the sick, the old and the dead. In the sources he is said to be seeking truth, knowledge and liberation. Several options can be defended: the search was prompted by suffering (option A), it aimed at truth and knowledge (option C), and it ended in enlightenment (option D). The printed age (30) also differs from the age of 29 often given in the tradition. For these reasons the question is left open. The intended answer is C.

**Intended answer: C (Truth and knowledge).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - buddhism

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these Buddhist Sects is practised in Japan?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Zen, a school of Mahayana Buddhism which stresses meditation, is the form of Buddhism strongly associated with Japan. Theravada is found mainly in Sri Lanka and South-East Asia, and the Tibetan form (also called Lamaism) is found in Tibet and the Himalayan region.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - buddhism

questions.enonce_markdown:
"Dharma" in the teachings of Buddha means:

*Options as printed:* A) Revelations   B) Instruction   C) Truth   D) Beliefs
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Buddhism, Dharma is the teaching of the Buddha, the doctrine and the path that he taught, and it is one of the Three Jewels (the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha). The word can also be translated as law, truth or the way things are, so both 'Instruction' (teaching) and 'Truth' can be defended, and the question is left open. The intended answer is B (instruction, that is, teaching).

**Intended answer: B (Instruction).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - buddhism

questions.enonce_markdown: Who founded Buddhism?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama, who was born into a princely family in the region of Lumbini (in present-day Nepal) and became known as the Buddha, 'the Awakened One', after his enlightenment. Amitabha is a Buddha of Mahayana devotion, and the Dalai Lama is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - buddhism

questions.enonce_markdown: Hindu pilgrimages and festivals are mostly around:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rivers are regarded as sacred in Hinduism, above all the Ganges, and many pilgrimages and festivals take place on their banks, for example bathing at Varanasi and at the Kumbh Mela. Temples and mountains are also pilgrimage places, but the option usually given in textbooks is rivers.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - hinduism

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the major feature of every Hindu home?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A Hindu home usually contains a shrine or a corner for worship (puja) with images of the family's deities, where daily worship is performed. A children's room is not a religious feature, a temple is a separate building, and a tambourine is not a standard feature of Hindu worship.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - hinduism

questions.enonce_markdown: The Union of the individual with the Supreme entity, Brahman, is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Hinduism the goal of life is moksha, liberation from the cycle of birth, death and rebirth, which is understood as the realisation of the union of the individual self (atman) with Brahman, the Supreme. Dharma is duty or righteous order, karma is the law of action and its results, and samsara is the cycle of rebirth itself.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - hinduism

questions.enonce_markdown:
Hindu belief about the Ganges is that:

*Options as printed:* A) It purifies and cures   B) It strengthens and kills   C) It blesses and cures   D) It liberates and produces
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hindus regard the Ganges as a sacred river whose water is believed to purify from sin and from ritual impurity, and many also believe that it has healing power. Option A states this. Option C ('blesses and cures') is close in meaning, and the sources do not allow a clear choice between the two wordings, so the question is left open. The intended answer is A.

**Intended answer: A (It purifies and cures).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - hinduism

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the first wife of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.S)?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first wife of the Prophet Muhammad was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a merchant who married him before the beginning of his mission and who was the first person to accept his message. Rukayyah was the name of one of his daughters, and Safiyyah and Aisha were wives of his later years.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - life of prophet muhammad

questions.enonce_markdown: The Qur'an was first revealed during the month of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Islamic tradition, the first revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad came in the month of Ramadan, on the night known as Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power), and this is why Ramadan is the month of fasting. Rajab, Dhul Qa'dah (printed 'Dzoul Qidda') and Muharram are other months of the Islamic calendar.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - the quran in islam

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are compilers of the authentic Hadiths except:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The authentic collections of Hadith, the sayings and actions of the Prophet, were compiled by scholars such as al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. Ibn Majah and Abu Da'ud are on this list, and 'Sahih Muslim' is the name of the collection of Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj. Ibn Hassan is not one of the compilers of the major collections, so it is the exception.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - islamic scriptures and law

questions.enonce_markdown: Voluntary charity in Islam is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sadaqa is the voluntary charity that a Muslim gives for the sake of God, in any amount and at any time. Zakat is the compulsory almsgiving, one of the Five Pillars, and Zakat-ul-fitr is the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan. 'Faqara' is not the name of a form of charity.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - social teachings of islam

questions.enonce_markdown: The most frequented Islamic sacred place of worship is in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Ka'bah in the Sacred Mosque of Mecca is the centre towards which Muslims turn in prayer, and it is the destination of the Hajj and the Umrah, so Mecca is the most visited Islamic holy place. Medina (the Prophet's mosque) and Jerusalem (al-Aqsa) are also holy places, and Mina is a site visited during the rites of the Hajj.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - islamic worship and practices

questions.enonce_markdown: A major Islamic feast which coincides with the yearly pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Eid al-Adha, the Feast of Sacrifice, is celebrated on the tenth day of Dhul Hijjah, during the Hajj, in memory of the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son in obedience to God. Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan, and the other two options are not major feasts of the Islamic calendar.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam

questions.enonce_markdown: What were the successors of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.S) called?
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the death of the Prophet Muhammad, his successors as leaders of the Muslim community were called caliphs (khulafa), beginning with Abu Bakr. Muslims hold that Muhammad is the last of the prophets, so no 'prophet' succeeds him; the imam leads the prayer, and the muezzin gives the call to prayer.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - islamic community and leadership

questions.enonce_markdown:
These ideals were taught by Muhammad to his followers except:

*Options as printed:* A) Quest for knowledge   B) Quest for uprightness   C) Quest of Jihad   D) Quest for peace
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Prophet's teaching encourages seeking knowledge, living uprightly and working for peace. Jihad means striving or struggle for the sake of God and is part of Islamic teaching, so it can be argued that all four options are teachings. If the question is read as asking for the item that is not presented as an ideal to be sought, the one that is usually singled out is the 'quest of Jihad', because it is a duty in specific circumstances. The wording is not clear enough for automatic marking, so the question is left open. The intended answer is C.

**Intended answer: C (Quest of Jihad).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - social teachings of islam

questions.enonce_markdown: The Islamic word for ritual purification before every prayer is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Wudu is the ritual washing of the hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head and feet that a Muslim performs before prayer. Tayammum (printed here as 'Tayammun') is the dry purification with clean earth or dust, which is allowed when water is not available, the ummah is the community of believers, and the qibla is the direction of Mecca towards which Muslims pray.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - prayer in islam

questions.enonce_markdown:
Who was the first companion of the holy prophet?

*Options as printed:* A) Ali Ibn Talib   B) Usman Ibu Affan   C) Unar El- Khattab   D) Abu Bakr sidiq
questions.corrige_markdown:
Many Muslims, especially in the Sunni tradition, name Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, the Prophet's closest friend and the first adult man to accept Islam, as the first companion and the first caliph. Other traditions give weight to Ali, the Prophet's cousin, who is remembered as the first young person to accept Islam. The printed question does not say which tradition it follows, so it is left open. The intended answer is D (Abu Bakr).

**Intended answer: D (Abu Bakr sidiq).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - life of prophet muhammad

questions.enonce_markdown: Women enjoy the following rights in Islam except:
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Islamic teaching, women have the right to inherit (Qur'an, chapter 4), to hold property, to seek education and to give their opinion in community affairs. According to the classical schools of law, a woman may lead other women in prayer, but she does not lead mixed congregations, so 'leading all congregational prayers' is the item which is not counted among these rights. Some modern scholars hold a different view, and this is why the answer is given according to the classical position.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - women in islam

questions.enonce_markdown: The chapters of the Qur'an are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Qur'an is divided into 114 chapters called surahs. Each surah is made up of verses called ayat (ayahs). Fiqh (printed 'Figh') is Islamic jurisprudence, and a raka'a is one unit of the Muslim prayer.

**Answer: B.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - the quran in islam

questions.enonce_markdown: The first constituted muslim community grew up in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the Hijrah (the migration from Mecca in 622 CE), the Prophet established at Medina the first organised Muslim community (ummah) with its own system of governance, its mosque and an agreement between its different groups. Mecca was the place of the first revelations, but the community was formally constituted at Medina. 'Kufr' means disbelief and is not a place, and Mina is a site of the Hajj.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - islamic community and leadership

questions.enonce_markdown: These are various forms of Judaism except:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conservative, Orthodox and Liberal (or Reform) are the names of recognised movements within modern Judaism. 'Mainstream' is a general description and is not the name of a movement, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: The Movement for the creation of a Jewish state in Palestine in 1948 was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Zionism is the movement which worked for a Jewish homeland and then for a Jewish state in Palestine, and the State of Israel was proclaimed in 1948. Fascism and Nazism are political ideologies, and anti-Semitism is hostility towards Jews.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: A prominent exponent of Jewish Orthodoxy in the 19th Century Germany was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Samson Raphael Hirsch (1808 to 1888), a rabbi in Germany, is the best known defender of Orthodox Judaism in nineteenth-century Germany, and he taught that loyalty to the Torah could be joined with modern education. The other names are not the usual answer to this question in textbooks.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - judaism

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is the  highest in heirachy in ATR ?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In African Traditional Religion (ATR), as described in general by scholars of the subject, the Supreme Being (God) is at the top of the hierarchy, followed by the divinities (the gods), the spirits and the ancestors, and then by the human beings who serve them, such as priests. These are general features, and the names and details differ from one people to another.

**Answer: D.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - atr supreme being and divinities

questions.enonce_markdown: Who are the living-dead in ATR?
questions.corrige_markdown:
'Living-dead' is the term used by the scholar John Mbiti for the ancestors: people who have died but who are still remembered by their families, and who are believed to remain part of the community and to watch over it. Spirits and deities are different categories of beings, and diviners are living specialists.

**Answer: A.**
themes: A Level Religious Studies - atr death and ancestors

questions.enonce_markdown:
The main duties of diviners in ATR is consultation with:

*Options as printed:* A) Sorcerers   B) Ancestors   C) The gods   D) Supreme Being
questions.corrige_markdown:
In many African societies the diviner is a specialist who consults the divinities and spirits in order to explain misfortune or illness and to give advice. Some diviners also communicate with the ancestors, so more than one option can be defended and the practice varies from one people to another. For this reason the question is left open. The intended answer is C (the gods, that is, the divinities and spirits).

**Intended answer: C (The gods).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - atr rain-makers and specialists

questions.enonce_markdown:
What can other world monotheistic religions learn from A.T.R?

*Options as printed:* A) Oral Tradition   B) Solidarity   C) Ancestral Worship   D) Juju manifestation
questions.corrige_markdown:
African Traditional Religion strongly stresses community, solidarity and mutual support, expressed in the saying 'I am because we are'. Other religions may be said to learn from this sense of solidarity. Oral tradition could also be named, and the question asks for an opinion more than for a fact, so it is left open. The intended answer is B.

**Intended answer: B (Solidarity).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - atr beliefs and practices

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these best describes A.T.R?
questions.corrige_markdown:
African Traditional Religion has no single codified text, since it is passed on by oral tradition, and it is a way of life lived in community, with no separation between what is religious and what is not. Many scholars also avoid describing it as simply polytheistic, since it recognises a Supreme Being, or as 'ancestor worship', since ancestors are usually honoured and not worshipped as gods. The description that is generally accepted is a communal lifestyle.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best way to prevent HIV in ATR is through:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks about the approach that fits the moral teaching of African Traditional Religion, which stresses chastity before marriage and faithfulness in marriage. Abstinence is the option that matches this teaching, and it is also the one that is given in the textbook answers to this question. Public health bodies also recommend education and the use of condoms, so this item reflects the viewpoint of the syllabus and not a medical ranking of methods.

**Answer: B.**
